findings.title: ActivityWeatherAnalyzer can_work ignores max_wind and min_visibility — authorizes crane/steel in unsafe weather
findings.description: WeatherThresholds defines max_wind and min_visibility for high-risk templates (crane_operations max_wind=30 / min_visibility=1.0, steel_erection max_wind=35, roofing max_wind=30). ActivityWeatherAnalyzer._calculate_impact only evaluates temperature and precipitation, then multiplies by primary_condition productivity factors. OpenWeatherMap parsing maps Mist/Fog→CLOUDY and never sets HIGH_WIND from wind_speed, so hourly wind_speed and visibility on DailyForecast/HourlyWeather are never consulted. ScheduleWeatherOptimizer.analyze_schedule / _analyze_activity call this gate to decide can_work and expected weather delays. Quick Start check_work_day correctly checks wind — the comprehensive path that agents are steered to does not.
findings.impact: Agents greenlight crane lifts and steel erection on clear/dry days with 65+ km/h winds or sub-1 km visibility → tip-over, load swing, struck-by fatality risk, and false 'no weather delay' schedule reports.
attack_path: Deploy ActivityWeatherAnalyzer + ScheduleWeatherOptimizer against live forecast.
Forecast day: primary_condition=CLEAR, precip=0, temp OK; hourly wind_speed=65 km/h, visibility=0.2 km (or high wind not mapped to HIGH_WIND).
Schedule crane_operations / steel_erection for that day.
_calculate_impact returns can_work=True, productivity=1.0, issues=[].
analyze_schedule reports zero weather delay; crews/crane dispatched.
evidence: WeatherThresholds.max_wind / min_visibility defined (lines ~329-336).
crane_operations thresholds max_wind=30, min_visibility=1.0 (lines ~413-418); steel_erection max_wind=35 (lines ~376-381).
_calculate_impact checks only temp_low/temp_high/precipitation_total + primary_condition factor — no wind/visibility (lines ~459-518).
HourlyWeather carries wind_speed and visibility (lines ~132-143) but unused in impact.
_map_condition maps Fog/Mist→CLOUDY; no HIGH_WIND from wind data (lines ~263-275).
ScheduleWeatherOptimizer._analyze_activity uses _calculate_impact for can_work (lines ~616-633).
PoC: clear/dry/65 km/h wind → crane and steel can_work=True, productivity=1.0.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not in already-reported list. Distinct from Quick Start check_work_day (which does check wind). Prior hunt near-miss was schedule-compression Low-risk text only, not this weather gate.

findings.title: Unknown activity_type fails open to interior_work (always can_work=True)
findings.description: ScheduleWeatherOptimizer._analyze_activity resolves the activity template via analyzer.activities.get(activity_type, ACTIVITY_TEMPLATES['interior_work']). Template keys are names like 'crane_operations', while ScheduledActivity also carries activity_id values like 'ACT-007'. Any misspelled, id-based, or custom activity_type silently falls back to interior_work (indoor=True), and _calculate_impact short-circuits to can_work=True / productivity=1.0 with no issues — including on extreme outdoor weather. suggest_reschedule correctly skips missing templates; analyze_schedule does not.
findings.impact: Outdoor critical work (crane, steel, roofing, concrete) scheduled under a wrong/unknown type is treated as weather-safe every day → unsafe mobilization and erased weather-delay exposure.
attack_path: ScheduledActivity.activity_type set to 'ACT-007' (id) or 'crane' (typo) instead of 'crane_operations'.
analyze_schedule → _analyze_activity → .get miss → interior_work.
indoor=True → can_work=True for every forecast day regardless of wind/rain/temp.
expected_delay stays 0; daily plan proceeds.
evidence: Fallback: activities.get(activity.activity_type, ACTIVITY_TEMPLATES.get('interior_work')) (lines ~616-620).
interior_work has indoor=True (lines ~427-434).
_calculate_impact early-return can_work=True when indoor (lines ~462-468).
PoC: lookup 'ACT-007' resolves to Interior Work → can_work=True in 65 km/h wind.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Separate fail-open from wind/visibility omission; same skill, different root cause (template resolution vs threshold evaluation).

findings.title: check_permit_status.is_valid ignores missing required documents; update_status forges ISSUED
findings.description: check_permit_status computes missing_documents into alerts only; is_valid is true for any ACTIVE/ISSUED permit that is not past expiry — even with zero submitted documents. Separately, PermitTracker.update_status accepts any PermitStatus with no state machine, document completeness check, fee check, or reviewer authZ, so DRAFT→ISSUED mints permit_number and expiry_date. Agents using is_valid or status==ISSUED as the work-authorization gate will clear construction without a complete (or real) permit package.
findings.impact: Unpermitted building/electrical/excavation work proceeds under a false valid/issued signal → stop-work orders, fines, insurance denial, and safety exposure from work that never received jurisdiction review.
attack_path: Path A: Construct/load Permit with status=ISSUED and submitted_documents=[]; required_documents still incomplete.
check_permit_status → alerts include missing_documents but is_valid=True.
Downstream agent/work-order gate trusts is_valid and authorizes site work.
Path B: create_application → update_status(..., PermitStatus.ISSUED) from DRAFT without submit_application or documents.
Application gains issued_date, permit_number, expiry; treated as issued for work release.
evidence: missing_docs only appended to alerts (lines ~78-81).
is_valid = status in ACTIVE/ISSUED and not expired — no document check (lines ~87-88).
PoC: ISSUED + empty submitted_documents → is_valid True with missing_documents alert.
update_status sets APPROVED/ISSUED with no prior-status or doc gate (lines ~356-380).
submit_application alone checks documents; update_status bypasses it.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior hunt skipped permit as soft near-miss. Re-evaluated with complete chain: skill-owned is_valid work-authorization boolean returns True despite missing required docs, plus unconstrained ISSUED forge. Not look-ahead constraint forge (different skill/gate).

findings.title: crash_schedule trusts caller is_critical and reports false achieved_reduction
findings.description: identify_critical_path does not compute float — it returns activities where caller-supplied is_critical is True. analyze_crash_options / crash_schedule only crash those flags. days_achieved increments once per crashed day on flagged activities even when project_duration (true CPM forward pass) does not drop. CompressionPlan.achieved_reduction uses days_achieved, not (original_duration - new_duration), and risk_assessment is hardcoded to 'Low risk - crashing uses proven methods'. Parallel-path schedules where the short path is mis-flagged critical produce claimed recovery with zero actual compression.
findings.impact: False schedule recovery hides liquidated-damages exposure, justifies wasted crash spend, and misleads owners/lenders that the deadline is recoverable when the true critical path was never shortened.
attack_path: Network: activity A duration=20 (true longest path, is_critical=False); parallel B duration=10 (is_critical=True wrongly).
crash_schedule(target_days=5) crashes B only; days_achieved=5.
calculate_project_duration still 20 (A dominates).
CompressionPlan reports achieved_reduction=5, new_project_duration=20, risk_assessment='Low risk…'.
PM/owner accepts recovery plan; no real days gained.
evidence: identify_critical_path: critical = [act.id for act in ... if act.is_critical] — no float calc (lines ~166-174).
add_activity accepts caller is_critical (lines ~105-119).
analyze_crash_options filters act.is_critical (lines ~180-181).
crash_schedule: days_achieved += 1 per crash day; achieved_reduction=days_achieved (lines ~227, 245-252).
risk_assessment hardcoded Low risk (line ~252).
PoC: claimed achieved_reduction=5, actual duration 20→20 (real reduction=0).
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior hunt only noted hardcoded Low-risk string as near-miss. This is the complete false-recovery chain via trusted is_critical + achieved_reduction not tied to CPM duration delta.

findings.title: assign_equipment never checks current status — double-books IN_USE assets
findings.description: assign_equipment appends a new Assignment and sets status=IN_USE without requiring status==AVAILABLE. An asset already IN_USE (or any other status) can be assigned to a second project/location the same day. get_available_equipment correctly filters AVAILABLE, but the mutating assign path does not. Distinct from already-reported schedule_maintenance/REPAIR never grounding equipment.
findings.impact: Same tower crane/excavator committed to two sites simultaneously → lift conflicts, phantom utilization, and crews mobilizing without equipment.
attack_path: assign_equipment(crane, Site A) → status IN_USE.
assign_equipment(crane, Site B) succeeds; assignments list length 2; status remains IN_USE.
Both project plans show the crane assigned; only one physical asset exists.
evidence: assign_equipment: no status==AVAILABLE guard (lines ~105-125).
get_available_equipment filters AVAILABLE (lines ~144-149) but assign does not use it.
PoC: two concurrent assignments on CR1 to Site A and Site B.
findings.why_not_duplicate: User excluded only Maintenance/REPAIR grounding. This is absence of IN_USE/AVAILABLE check on assign (double-book), not the REPAIR status bug. Distinct from resource-pool-optimizer max-not-sum (different skill).
